## 3. This cycle's attacks

1. E-UTF8 prefix-decode formula (§4.2) — REFUTED live (probe 91). The
   hypothesis: where the first invalid byte is a continuation slot,
   `e.start` points inside the sequence, so `data[:e.start].decode()`
   ends with a dangling lead and raises a second UnicodeDecodeError,
   routing an invalid-UTF-8 input to E-NET. Live on 3.13.5: CPython
   reports `e.start` at the LEAD byte for every mid-sequence corpus
   (b'a\xe2\x28' → start=1 cites 0xe2; b'\xf0\x9f\x28' → start=0 cites
   0xf0; truncated-at-EOF → start at lead, reason 'data'; overlong →
   lead), so the prefix always decodes and E-UTF8 always fires. 10/10
   corpora E-UTF8, 0 E-NET. The spec's sentence stands.
2. Caller-controlled path classes (§6.1 "no type check", §4.2 "Any
   OSError") — CONTRACTED (probe 92, after the stub was made
   spec-literal with the at-open OSError→E-WRITE mapping §2.2 pins):
   directory-as-input → E-READ; directory-as-output and empty-string
   output → E-WRITE (at-open OSErrors, no compensation, target
   byte-untouched); raw non-UTF-8 byte paths round-trip via
   surrogateescape (output run succeeds, input run E-READ); NUL-in-argv
   is closed by execve itself (spawner ValueError) — the tool can never
   receive such a path. No catalog gap.
3. Default-config stderr wire form for argv-borne lone surrogates
   (§6.3 encoding-scope paragraph; §12 'error catalog' row) — GAP FOUND
   (probe 93, W1): the spec anticipates non-verbatim wire bytes only for
   environment-OVERRIDDEN encodings, but a raw-byte filename in argv
   (legal on Linux, decoded via surrogateescape) puts a lone surrogate in
   the message STRING, and DEFAULT sys.stderr (errors=backslashreplace)
   transliterates it to `\udcff` with no override and no raise. → F-01.
4. §4.3 interface/prose signature mismatch — FOUND (probe 92 P2a/P2b):
   the Interface line declares `parse(text: str) -> list[dict[str, str]]`
   while the very next prose sentence says "(`parse(text, input_name)`)". → F-02.
5. Evidence-hygiene class (mechval C17, this cycle's whole reason):
   re-verified independently — grep for unannotated `spec/1[0-5]` cites:
   none; the single `spec/15` mention sits inside its own HISTORICAL
   annotation; gate 90 reports 0 stale cites; gates 84/85/86/87/88 all
   green when re-run by this reviewer; behavioral 66 re-run green
   (27/27); permanent 14/15 re-run green. One residue: the probes-row
   sentence "Behavioral probes 66/77 and the permanent 13/14/15 are
   untouched and LIVE" is asserted by the header, but gate 88's LIVE
   list covers only 13/77 — 66, 14, 15 are claimed LIVE with no
   liveness-checking check inside the v16 battery (this reviewer ran
   them green manually; the gap is gate coverage, not truth). → F-03.

## 4. Findings

### F-01 [P2|boundary-input/wire-form|needs-user:false]
- section/artifact: spec/16-spec-v16.md §6.3 encoding-scope paragraph
  ("Encoding scope of the verbatim rule"); §12 glossary "error catalog"
  row ("default CPython stderr preserves UTF-8 verbatim"); §6.4 stderr
  cell (same sentence).
- claim or missing contract: the spec states the verbatim STRING rule and
  then scopes all non-verbatim WIRE outcomes to environment-controlled
  encodings — "the BYTES observed on the wire additionally depend on the
  interpreter's stderr encoding, which is environment-controlled
  (PYTHONIOENCODING, locale), not tool-controlled: on default CPython
  stderr the Thai-name E-DUP message reaches the wire as verbatim UTF-8
  under C and UTF-8 locales alike". The implied default-configuration
  guarantee ("default → verbatim") is falsifiable: it holds only for
  messages that are UTF-8-encodable as str.
- evidence: probe 93 W1 (live, default env, no overrides): a Linux
  filename containing a raw non-UTF-8 byte (`out\xff.json`) reaches argv
  as the surrogateescape-decoded str `out\udcff.json`; the E-READ
  message STRING carries the lone surrogate verbatim (W3), and the
  default sys.stderr (encoding utf-8, errors backslashreplace — W4)
  emits `csv2json: error: cannot read in\udcff.csv: No such file or
  directory\n` as the literal ASCII bytes `in\udcff.csv` —
  transliterated, not verbatim, with no override in play and no raise.
  Control W2: the Thai path stays raw UTF-8 on the wire (the glossary
  sentence is true for encodable messages).
- minimal counterexample: (1) `printf 'id,name\n1,x\n' > good.csv`;
  (2) create a raw-byte name: the file `in\xff.csv` does not exist;
  (3) run `python csv2json.py $'in\xff.csv' out.json` on default CPython
  (Linux); (4) argv[1] decodes to `in\udcff.csv` (surrogateescape);
  (5) read_raw raises ENOENT → E-READ message STRING contains the
  surrogate (verbatim, per the tool's contract); (6) the single stderr
  write puts `in\udcff.csv` (backslash-escaped) on the wire — the §6.3
  sentence's "on default CPython stderr ... reaches the wire as verbatim
  UTF-8" class silently excludes this input, and §6.3's only enumerated
  non-verbatim triggers (PYTHONIOENCODING overrides) do not cover it.
- impact: bounded — one stderr line's wire form for raw-byte paths; exit
  code, catalog class, message STRING, and all other inputs unchanged.
  A tester asserting default-wire-verbatim for a raw-byte-path corpus
  would flap for environment reasons — exactly the confusion the
  encoding-scope paragraph exists to prevent (adv-c9 F-04's class, one
  input class short).
- required disposition: extend the §6.3 encoding-scope paragraph (and
  the §12 glossary mirror) by one sentence: wire bytes are verbatim only
  for messages that are UTF-8-encodable; an argv-borne raw byte (Linux
  surrogateescape path) puts a lone surrogate in the message string and
  DEFAULT stderr's backslashreplace handler transliterates it (no
  override, no raise) — same environment-controlled class, no tool
  action. No behavior change; wording only.
- decision owner: spec-designer.
- verification required: none blocking (P2); re-run 93 after the fold.

### F-02 [P2|internal-consistency|needs-user:false]
- section/artifact: spec/16-spec-v16.md §4.3 Interface bullet.
- claim or missing contract: the Interface line pins
  `parse(text: str) -> list[dict[str, str]]`, raising FieldError — one
  method, five behavior clauses; the immediately following prose
  sentence reads "The input path name is passed for message construction
  (`parse(text, input_name)`); nothing else is configurable." The two
  declarations disagree on the signature arity.
- evidence: probe 92 P2a/P2b — both greps hit the same §4.3 block; the
  Interface line and the parenthetical sit four lines apart.
- minimal counterexample: an implementor following the Interface bullet
  builds `def parse(text)`; the message templates they must raise
  (E-EMPTY `csv2json: error: <in>: file is empty ...`, E-COUNT, E-UQ,
  E-UTF8-adjacent parse classes) all interpolate `<in>`, which under the
  Interface-arity build has no source inside parse — the prose sentence
  supplies it, the Interface line forbids it. Both shapes "work" (pass
  the input name via a closure/global is a third), so the spec names two
  conforming signatures for the same stage with no rule choosing.
- impact: bounded — local implementation detail; no observable behavior
  difference (messages identical either way). But it is a
  normative-signature contradiction inside one bullet, the exact class
  mechval structural checks exist to catch, surviving 16 cycles.
- required disposition: one-line edit — either the Interface line
  becomes `parse(text, input_name)` (matching the prose and §2.2's
  responsibility table, which already implies message construction with
  the input name), or the prose drops the parenthetical. Prefer the
  former (the messages need the name).
- decision owner: spec-designer.
- verification required: none (P2); grep the fixed line in the next
  gate re-aim.

## 5. Refuted attacks (negative results, kept as evidence)

1. E-UTF8 prefix crash (§4.2 formula) — REFUTED (probe 91, 10 corpora).
   CPython 3.13.5 points e.start at the sequence LEAD for invalid
   continuation bytes, truncated sequences (reason 'data'), and overlong
   forms; the prefix decode never raises; E-UTF8 fires 10/10. The
   formula's wording "the valid-UTF-8 prefix is itself decoded" is
   accurate on this interpreter. Note for the file: appendix/48b P1's
   docstring hypothesized the continuation-byte landing; its checks were
   correctly written to accept either outcome; no finding was filed then
   and none is warranted now (single-interpreter evidence: 3.13.5 is the
   only interpreter on this host; NFR-002's 3.9 floor cannot be
   re-verified here — T-C14's skip-with-warning convention applies).
2. NUL-in-argv path (§6.1 "no type check") — UNREACHABLE (probe 92 P1z):
   execve rejects NUL-bearing argv at spawn; the tool never sees it.
3. Directory/empty-string/raw-byte path classes — CONTRACTED (probe 92):
   all land in cataloged OSError classes (E-READ / at-open E-WRITE per
   D-46); surrogateescape round-trips raw-byte names losslessly for
   open(); no E-NET leakage.
4. Stale-cite / annotation-truth class (the mechval-c15 F-01 family) —
   CLEAN: gate 90 (0 stale cites), grep for unannotated spec/1x cites
   (none), gates 84/85/86/87/88 re-run green by this reviewer, 66/77
   behavioral probes re-run green.
5. Write-stage window arithmetic (D-43/D-46/D-48/D-50/D-53/D-54/D-57) —
   no new residue class found: every window this reviewer re-derived
   (second-non-OSError inside the arm; KI/MemoryError inside open();
   encode-before-open; at-open OSError) maps onto a recorded decision
   and R-n risk. The residue-class demotion policy (cycle >= 5) applies
   and no unrecorded twin window was found this cycle.
